claim: For a field R of prime characteristic p, if every finite subgroup of a word-hyperbolic group G is a p-group, the BLR hyperbolic-group result gives only idempotents 0 and 1 in RG. In particular, this applies to R=F_2 and torsion-free word-hyperbolic G.
exact_assumptions: G satisfies the K-theoretic Farrell-Jones conjecture with coefficients in every ring; BLR's main theorem supplies this for word-hyperbolic G
R is a field of prime characteristic p
every finite subgroup of G is a p-group
no soficity assumption in the field case

primary_source.citation: A. Bartels, W. Lueck, H. Reich, The K-theoretic Farrell-Jones conjecture for hyperbolic groups, Invent. Math. 172(1) (2008), 29-70, DOI 10.1007/s00222-007-0093-7
primary_source.dates: arXiv first submitted 2007-01-16; journal 2008; source checked 2026-10-08
primary_source.locator: main theorem and Applications, Kaplansky Conjecture for prime characteristic, PDF p. 3

derivation_to_N129_conflict: N129's ab=1, ac=0, c!=0 imply ba!=1 and ba!=0; e=1-ba is a nonzero idempotent unequal to 1. This contradicts BLR under N129's claimed torsion-free word-hyperbolic and F_2 hypotheses.
scope_limit: This audit identifies an incompatibility; it does not locate the failed N129 proof premise or replay the BLR proof.

claim: The same authors' companion paper separately says Formanek's positive-characteristic theorem applies to torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups over fields, so all group-ring idempotents are trivial. This is distinct from generic Theorem 1.12.
exact_assumptions: F is a field of prime characteristic p
there are no g!=1 and k>=1 with g conjugate to g^(p^k)
torsion-free word-hyperbolic groups are stated to satisfy these conditions

primary_source.citation: A. Bartels, W. Lueck, H. Reich, On the Farrell-Jones Conjecture and its applications, J. Topol. 1(1) (January 2008), 57-86, DOI 10.1112/jtopol/jtm008
primary_source.dates: publisher reports first published online 2007-10-28; issue January 2008; source checked 2026-10-08
primary_source.locator: Theorem 1.12 p. 62 (generic result); section 1.6, pp. 63-64 (Formanek/hyperbolic application)

clarification: Theorem 1.12 alone has additional K0 and stable-finiteness/characteristic-zero/sofic alternatives. The later explicit Formanek/hyperbolic application and the separate prime-characteristic corollary in the hyperbolic paper do cover the N129 case.
